offence_severity: imprisonment for life or rigorous imprisonment for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine
physical_harm: Burn injuries on both legs, 45-48% of body burned, loss of one leg
number_of_offences: Three offences/counts charged, two finally upheld
premeditation_planning: Court found premeditation/planning as the accused planned the murder
key_evidence_accepted: The complainant himself, an injured witness, was accepted as an extremely valuable evidence in the criminal trial. The injuries sustained by the complainant matched the prosecution's case, and there were burn injuries on both his legs and a strong ligature mark on his neck, which supported the prosecution's claim of attempted strangulation.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses, particularly the complainant, as credible despite his injuries and the traumatic nature of the incident. The court emphasized that the complainant's statement, although given under distressing circumstances, was not doubted unless there was compelling evidence to the contrary.
bail_history: Order dated 17.09.2019 of this Court up to the extent of suspending the sentence of appellant Neeraj Sharma and granting him bail is hereby vacated. The bail bonds of appellant Neeraj Sharma stand cancelled
trial_duration: Trial Court passed its Judgement dated 03.01.2015; High Court of Chhattisgarh at Bilaspur in CRA No.200 of 2015; Supreme Court decision on 03 January 2024
legal_representation: Sameer Shrivastava, Ms. Yashika Varshney, Mrs. Priyanka Shrivastava, Mrs. Sangeeta, Shivendra Dixit, Advs. for the Appellant; Sumeer Sodhi, Ms. Bhawana Mapwal, Advs. for the Respondent
investigation_status: Chargesheet filed against the three accused under Sections 120B, 364A, 307, 392/397 and in the alternative section 394 of IPC
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction and sentence of the appellants upheld; High Court: Dismissed the Criminal Appeal of the present appellants, upholding the conviction and sentence of the trial court; Supreme Court: Partly allowed the appeals, set aside the conviction under Section 364A and affirmed the rest of the conviction and sentence
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellants abducted Arjit Sharma for ransom, attempted to murder him, and tried to dispose of his body by burning it. They claimed the victim sustained grievous injuries, including burn injuries and loss of a leg, and that the accused looted his belongings.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the prosecution failed to establish the demand of ransom, which is a necessary ingredient for conviction under Section 364-A of the IPC. They also contended that the victim's statement, while important, did not contain any mention of ransom and that the supplementary statement about ransom was not reliable.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that for an offence under Section 364-A of the IPC, the prosecution must prove kidnapping or abduction coupled with a demand of ransom and a threat to life, which was not established in this case.
precedent_relied_upon: Rajesh v. State of Madhya Pradesh, 2023 SCC OnLine SC 1202; Shaik Ahmed v. State of Telangana (2021) 9 SCC 59; Balu Sudam Khalde v. State of Maharashtra 2023 SCC OnLine SC 355
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed for the offence under Section 364 of the IPC, which covers abduction in order to murder, as the prosecution failed to establish the ransom demand required for Section 364-A.
other_sentence_order: Compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- was directed to be paid by the State of Chhattisgarh to the victim under Section 357A of the Cr.PC.
